share_of_the_estate_that_stays.basis: the scout's bracket from two derivations; NO source splits energy by consumer against business. Enterprise alone is 25 % and stays. Two large consumer operators counted wholly as consumer are 12 % of the total.
share_of_the_estate_that_stays.depends_on: what 'replace the internet entirely' includes; if enterprise, government and science computing also go, this input is a definition and is near zero
share_of_the_estate_that_stays.resolved_as: Case A (central): 0.6 (0.45 to 0.75). Case B (counterfactual): rented business work relocated at 1.4 to 4 times. See 'businesses'.

of_consumer_work_the_share_that_vanishes.basis: video is 54 to 57 % of downstream BYTES and relocates, but its data-centre energy is about 1.3 Wh per viewing hour, a few per cent of the estate: bytes are not data-centre energy

edge_against_data_centre.scout: two terms: a marginal ratio of 0.1 to 1 on devices ALREADY ON, plus the fixed draw of anything ADDED (a two-bay home storage box is 39 to 129 kWh a year, the order of the whole per-user baseline)
edge_against_data_centre.basis: each published 'edge wins' result assumed the gateway already on and priced the data centre at 15 to 77 times the 2020 measured cost per bit

ai_share_of_the_estate.scout: 0.15 is the IEA's 2024 proxy without cooling overhead; 17 to 21 % with it; 23 % in the US in 2023; about 19 % in 2026 and 32 % in 2030 at the IEA's rates (the scout's arithmetic)

device_against_data_centre_inference.scout: same model: 3 to 30 (laptop 3 to 10, phone 10 to 30; never measured like for like). As served (a small device model against a hosted frontier model): 0.3 to 5. Frontier models and training cannot move to homes at all.

businesses.how_the_constitution_models_a_business: an affiliation: 'a room that acts as one voice', a body on the network that runs nodes it owns ('a node is a device or server you own'); one of the five circles

case_A_central.statement: organisations' work stays on servers, owned or rented, placed by the market at about today's efficiency; the share of the estate that stays is 0.45 to 0.75 (centre 0.6)
case_A_central.basis: enterprise-owned is 0.25 (IEA 2025, read at source); the rest is the scout's bracket, unsourced

case_B_counterfactual.statement: no large facilities: rented business work moves to organisations' own premises
case_B_counterfactual.efficiency_ratio: 1.4 (overhead alone: PUE 1.54 against about 1.1) to about 4 (a vendor-commissioned claim of 3.2 to 4.1); near 1 for best practice
case_B_counterfactual.basis: web search results, not read at source: IEA cooling shares 7 % against over 30 %; Uptime 2025 average PUE 1.54; utilisation about 65 % cloud against 12 to 18 % on premises (2014, as quoted by a vendor)

businesses.not_found: any split of a hyperscale operator's capacity or energy between its own consumer services and its business customers

ai_as_a_mix_across_tiers.the_leads_definition: a mixture of on-device, edge, prosumer, office appliance, servers, etc. - the market optimizes

energy_by_tier.basis: one operator's disclosure, 2025; fell 33 times in a year

energy_by_tier.note: no measured J per token or idle draw for a single-GPU office box was found; at low load it cannot batch and sits near the laptop

same_model_laptop_against_data_centre.one_request_at_a_time: the data centre is 1.6 to 2.3 times better per joule
same_model_laptop_against_data_centre.together: about 18 to 46 times against a batched data centre (the scout's arithmetic on the two factors)
same_model_laptop_against_data_centre.source: Saad-Falcon et al., arXiv 2511.07885, November 2025, read by the scout
same_model_laptop_against_data_centre.correction: the scout's first report said no like-for-like measurement existed and gave 'laptop 3 to 10'; that was wrong and is corrected in its report

ai_as_a_mix_across_tiers.what_decides_efficiency: model size and how full the machine is, not where it sits

routing.finding: sending easy queries to small local models saves 48 to 80 % of energy against sending everything to a frontier model, and the saving comes from model size, not hardware
routing.capability: local models answer 71 to 89 % of single-turn queries correctly (23 % in 2023)

what_vanishes.requested_generative_inference_share_of_: about 5 to 20 % (the scout's bound from operators' own figures)
what_vanishes.note: the often-quoted 'inference is 60 to 90 %' figures are from 2019 to 2021 and are mostly ranking inference

agents.tokens_per_task: an agent about 4 times chat; multi-agent about 15 times (one provider, June 2025, read)
agents.note: per person per day is unmeasured; energy rises less than tokens because agent traffic is mostly input

ai_as_a_mix_across_tiers.zero_data_retention: prompts and responses are not stored after processing; metadata, safety exceptions and in-memory caching remain; by default API data is not trained on. On the hosted tier it removes almost no energy: what vanishes is the platforms' own ranking, advertising and training.
ai_as_a_mix_across_tiers.suggested_inputs: energy per token by tier with model size and a utilisation term; the local share swept from 0 to 0.8; the vanish share of AI 0.2 to 0.6; the agent multiple 1, 2, 5, 15

idle_draw_by_tier.value: idle reserve is about 10 % of 0.24 Wh per prompt
idle_draw_by_tier.trust: high, and it fell 33 times in a year

ai_as_a_mix_across_tiers.idle_decides_the_home_and_office_tiers: The scout's arithmetic, with the query count assumed: a 5 W box answering 50 queries a day spends 96 % of its energy idle, 2.5 Wh per query, ten times the hosted figure. A desktop with a high-end card idling at an assumed 80 W is 700 kWh a year. A tier that is on FOR inference carries its idle draw; a tier that is on anyway does not.
